fixes.explanation: Remembering is a sweet verb, friend, but it isn't the one Paul uses. He asks, “Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?” Notice he doesn't just state it. He asks it, and he hands the room the hard part. I bet that's a question nobody wanted to answer out loud.

A new name sounds lovely, friend, but it isn't on the list. Jesus says they may receive “…forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.” Forgiveness first, then an inheritance, and it's shared among those sanctified by faith in Him. I'd say that's already a full box.

A long life would be nice, friend, and I'd happily take some extra years myself. But Jesus doesn't mention it in this line. He says they receive “…forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.” Forgiveness and an inheritance, and I think that's the better deal.

Journeys aren't what Festus names, friend. He exclaims in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!” Of all the things he could have blamed, he picks Paul's learning. I bet Paul had heard some creative accusations by then, but that one has to be near the top.
